brand_notes.fabric: brands.json's brand string is 'X-Pac / Ecopak (visible ripstop grid, dye-sublimation prints)'. Both confirmed VERBATIM on the maker's own pages: the Gila Dry Bag is built from 'Ecopak or Xpac' with 'water-resistant seam-taped construction'; the Alamo Top Tube Bag and Salsa Cutthroat Frame Bag are both specced as 'Ecopak Ultra 200X' / 'Ultra 200X Black Magic' (Ecopak's branded denier-weight naming). One exception found: the Bismarck Bottle Bucket is described by a third-party review (bikepacking.com) as 'two layers of Cordura, a padded insert, and a durable Hypalon bottom pan' — Cordura, not X-Pac/Ecopak, and not confirmed on Rogue Panda's own product page (which does not state a fabric at all for this SKU). Flagged as an exception, not asserted as the brand default.
brand_notes.method: No local photos exist for this brand (assets/products/ has no rogue-panda-designs folder). roguepanda.com is Shopify and completely open to WebFetch — no Cloudflare/bot-blocking encountered, unlike Wizard Works. A real, repeated finding: Rogue Panda publish detailed VOLUME and WEIGHT tables for every stock size of their frame bags and seat bag, but literally NO linear dimensions (length/width/height) anywhere on the product pages, the dedicated 'Frame Bag Guides' blog series, or their knowledge base — confirmed by direct page fetch, not assumed. The one general construction fact they do publish repeatedly (product knowledge base AND the custom-frame-bags page, independently) is that their frame bags run '2.75 inches wide at the edges, but will expand to 4-5 inches wide in the middle' — a genuine brand-wide gusset-taper spec, used below to correct two records where the previous pass had used the narrower edge figure instead of the wider (and, per the dimension rule, correct) middle figure.

products.name: Gila Dry Bag
products.dims_raw: Product page spec table, Flat Bar / Large: '8.5" diameter, 22" stuffed length, 33" flat length'; Volume 18 liters (Flat Bar, Large).
products.dims_note: Dual-rolltop dry-bag tube, same construction class as Alpkit's Airlok Dual elsewhere in this catalogue: the maker publishes BOTH a 'flat length' (33in — the sewn tube laid out flat before either end is rolled, a fabrication-pattern measurement per this project's established Airlok Dual precedent) and a 'stuffed length' (22in — the packed, in-use length with both rolltops closed). Used 'stuffed length' directly for len, per that same precedent, NOT the 'flat length'. 22in = 55.88cm, corrected from the previously-stored 53cm (which matched neither published figure exactly and is untraceable). Diameter 8.5in = 21.59cm, essentially unchanged from the previously-stored 21.5.

geometry.notes: Straight fabric tube, dual independent rolltops (one at each end) for the flat-bar harness version. HDPE stiffeners in the rolltops aid one-handed closure. No photo for this brand — shape read from description only, though 'straight dry-bag tube' is a very low-risk inference for this product class.

closure.hardware: dual rolltop (flat-bar version) with HDPE stiffeners; the drop-bar version instead uses a single-side rolltop with compression-style buckles clipping across the bag

details.fabric: Ecopak or X-Pac (Ultra 400X weight referenced in the weight table) — matches brand_notes.fabric
details.notes: Contrast webbing on the flat-bar version. Designed for handlebar mounting via a separate harness system (e.g. Rogue Panda's own harness or a third-party cradle), not modelled here — the dry bag itself carries only compression/girth straps.

mount.notes: Sits in a separate handlebar harness (not included/modelled), which does the actual bar clamping; the dry bag itself is a passive tube inside it. Clearance not established — no photo.

products.name: Alamo Top Tube Bag
products.dims_raw: Product page: Gordo size is '3.5 inches wide and 4 inches tall in the front, and 9 inches long. It tapers to 2.5 inches wide and 2.5 inches tall at the rear.' Gordito Grande 'same dimensions as the Gordo but 11 inches long instead of 9 inches.' Capacity 1.75L.
products.dims_note: Front (larger) end used per the tapered-axis rule: 11in length = 27.94cm (len, matches previously-stored 27.9 exactly), 3.5in front width = 8.89cm (wid, matches 8.9 exactly), 4in front height = 10.16cm (hgt, matches previously-stored 10.2 closely). All three independently maker-confirmed, no correction needed — this record was already right.

geometry.notes: Front (nose, toward the saddle) is the full 3.5in/4in width/height; tapers to 2.5in/2.5in at the rear (toward the head tube) — taper ratio 2.5/4 = 0.625 on height, 2.5/3.5 = 0.71 on width; recorded as a single linear taper using the height ratio as the dominant figure.

details.fabric: Ecopak Ultra 200X (in-stock colourway 'Black Magic') — matches brand_notes.fabric
details.notes: HDPE side panels for structure. Cable port for charging electronics. 'Combined strap-bolt attachment system' using TPU straps and spacers — two 9in straps and one 15in strap included per bag.

mount.notes: Sits on the top tube just behind the head tube, wide nose toward the saddle. Clearance not established — no photo.

products.name: Salsa Cutthroat Stock Frame Bag
products.dims_raw: Product page: 58cm size = 12 liters, 13.4oz/380g (no linear dimensions). Separate 'Salsa Cutthroat Frame Bag Guide' blog page: table of Full Frame Bag volumes by size — 52cm 5L, 54cm 7L, 56cm 10L, 58cm 14L, 60cm 18L — CONFLICTS with the product page's 58cm=12L. Rogue Panda's own knowledge base/custom-bag copy (repeated on two separate pages): frame bags run 'about 2.75 inches wide at the edges, but will expand to 4-5 inches wide in the middle.'
products.dims_note: Rogue Panda publish NO linear dimensions for any stock frame bag anywhere I could find (product page, size guide blog, or knowledge base) — confirmed directly, not assumed. len (55cm) and hgt (36cm) are UNCHANGED from the prior pass's reconstruction, calibrated against this catalogue's own peer 12L full-frame bags (Rockgeist Gravel 52Hz Large 56x36x6.5, WOHO XTouring Full Frame Dry L 50x36x8) — kept as a reasonable low-confidence estimate, not independently re-derived here. wid CORRECTED from 7cm to 12.7cm: the prior pass used the 2.75in EDGE figure (6.985cm≈7), but per this project's tapered-axis rule the LARGER value belongs in dims_cm — the maker's own 4-5in MIDDLE figure — so wid is now the max of that range (5in=12.7cm), with the taper down to 7cm at the tube-contact edges recorded in geometry.taper. Volume check: 55x12.7x36=25,146cc=25.1L vs published 12L is a 2.1x fill ratio — high but still under the ~2.2x ceiling this catalogue treats as plausible for a soft full-frame bag. The 12L-vs-14L conflict between Rogue Panda's own two pages is unresolved; kept 12L since that is the specific product-page/SKU figure this catalogue entry represents.

geometry.notes: Gusseted frame bag: ~2.75in (7cm) thick at the top-tube/down-tube contact edges, expanding to 4-5in (10-12.7cm) in the middle for capacity — a genuine maker-published brand-wide construction fact (see brand_notes), applied here since it directly explains why a flat 7cm width under-fills the published 12L volume. Designed for current-generation V2/V3 Salsa Cutthroat frames specifically.

closure.hardware: #10 YKK molded-tooth zippers (non-waterproof); second zipper creates a 'Double Decker' internal divider on all sizes except 52cm

details.notes: Bolt-on / direct-mount attachment using custom thumb screws into the Cutthroat's own frame bosses (not a strap-on generic bag) — closest available closure category (zip_two_way) captures the double-zip 'Double Decker' compartment, but the mount itself is bolt-on, see mount.notes. Sizes 54-60cm fit a 3-liter Apidura hydration bladder in the lower compartment. Left-side slip pocket for phone/wallet.

mount.notes: Bolt-on direct-mount into the Cutthroat's own frame bosses via custom thumb screws — NOT a universal strap-on bag, specific to this frame's bolt pattern. Clearance not established — no photo.

products.name: Ripsey Seat Bag V2
products.dims_raw: Product page publishes volume ('8 Liters'), weight ('16oz with Ultra 200X dry bag'), load rating ('6lbs/3kg recommended maximum'), and mounting clearances ('3 inches minimum tire clearance at half capacity'), but NO length/width/height figures anywhere on the page — checked directly (curl, full page text), not assumed from a summary.
products.dims_note: No maker linear dims found. dims_cm carried over unchanged from brands.json ('est': false, implying a prior maker source I could not independently verify). Box check: 35x15x15=7875cc=7.875L against a published 8L is a 0.98x ratio — unusually tight even for a packed dry-bag shape (this project's own guidance expects roughly 1.0-2.5x), which is itself a mild reason for caution rather than confidence. verified is false and confidence low specifically on the dims triple.

geometry.notes: Clamp-mounted dry-bag seat pack (not a simple strap-on holster) — see mount for the clamp system. No photo for this brand; shape read from description only.

closure.hardware: waterproof dry-bag zipper (maker copy: 'burliest zippers in the world'), not a rolltop

details.fabric: Ecopak Ultra 200X standard (in-stock: 'Ultra 400X Black Magic'); 'dozens of fabrics' available custom — matches brand_notes.fabric
details.notes: Patent-pending two-point mechanical clamp mount, NOT webbing straps: a rotating/sliding-shim saddle clamp (half-pipe ABS shims, standard clamp 40-64mm rail distance, wide clamp 64-88mm rail distance) plus a separate 31.6mm aluminum seatpost clamp with snap-in shims (fits 25-26mm dropper stanchions and 27.2mm rigid posts), CNC-machined buckles by Austere Manufacturing. Optional replaceable skid plate available. 6lb/3kg maximum recommended load.

mount.notes: Mechanical clamp system (see details), not webbing straps — nose is rigidly clamped rather than cinched. Maker states 3in (76mm) minimum tire clearance at half capacity.

products.name: Bismarck Bottle Bucket
products.dims_raw: Maker's own page publishes no dimensions or volume figure at all — sizing is described only as 'any bike bottle will work... any bottle you can fit in a bottle cage will work,' i.e. it is sized to fit a generic bottle+cage, not a fixed internal volume.
products.dims_note: Inherently a bottle-cage-shaped open-top holster with no fixed capacity by design — there is no maker figure to verify against. dims_cm carried over unchanged from brands.json, which already flagged this as 'est': true. Plausible against a typical 24oz bottle (the maker's own reference bottle, a 24oz Breakaway, is roughly 7cm diameter x 20cm tall) but this is a sanity check, not a citation.

geometry.notes: Open-top cylinder built around a bottle cage per maker copy ('built up on a bottle cage to allow quick, one-handed operation'). No photo for this brand; shape read from description only.

details.fabric: Two layers of Cordura with a padded insert and a Hypalon bottom pan, per a third-party review — NOT confirmed as X-Pac/Ecopak, an exception to brand_notes.fabric
details.notes: 'Ultra-Secure Attachments' via fork-crown tensioning is the stated stability mechanism — explicitly 'no stem strap needed.' Three mesh pockets with tight elastic for bars/gels/drink mixes. Open top (no drawstring or flap), the bottle cage itself is the retention mechanism.

mount.notes: Two short TPU straps to the handlebar plus one longer strap tensioned down to the fork crown — an unusual three-point mount (most stem bags mount only to the bar/stem/headset). Clearance not established — no photo.

products.name: Custom Half Frame Bag
products.dims_raw: Custom Frame Bags page: 'We have over 1000 frames on file - and if we don't have your bike saved, we can make you a bag with just a photo.' Standard bags run '2.75 inches wide at the edges, but will expand to 4-5 inches wide in the middle'; different widths available 'for an additional charge.' Options explicitly include 'Wedge or Partial frame bag' as distinct configurations from a Full frame bag.
products.dims_note: Made-to-measure per customer bike, like Rogue Panda's stock frame bags but with no size chart at all — there is no fixed length/height to cite. len (40cm) and hgt (12cm) are UNCHANGED placeholder figures carried from brands.json representing a generic mid-size half-frame bag (not a real SKU), kept only because this catalogue slot needs a representative geometry. wid CORRECTED from 7cm to 12.7cm using the same brand-wide gusset-taper logic applied to the Salsa Cutthroat record in this file (max of the published 4-5in middle-width range), with the 7cm edge figure moved into geometry.taper where it belongs. Do not treat len/hgt as a real product measurement — they are an unsourced generic placeholder, flagged accordingly.

geometry.notes: Same gusseted construction as Rogue Panda's stock frame bags (2.75in edges expanding to 4-5in middle) — see brand_notes and the Salsa Cutthroat record in this file for the same correction applied consistently.

closure.hardware: 'burliest zippers in the world' per maker copy — burly zip, no velcro alternative offered

details.fabric: Over 50 standard fabrics offered (X-Pac/Ecopak per brand_notes), plus custom prints
details.notes: Internal loops in the top-tube seam for strapping tent poles/pumps to the top of the bag. Light-coloured interior panels (for finding items inside). One hydration/cable port near the head tube included as standard on all Rogue Panda frame bags.

mount.notes: Bespoke fit to the customer's own frame triangle; geometry above is generic/indicative only, not a real product size. Clearance not established — no photo.
